title: Rate limiter window edge-case causing attribution gaps during tenant migration
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers have reported that the Console per-model breakdown shows sudden drops for a small number of final-minute requests during tenant migrations between shard groups. Root cause hypothesis: an edge-case in the global rate-limiter window boundary combined with tenant migration logic causes last-second tokens to be dropped from the billing pipeline rather than queued and forwarded, resulting in undercounting in reconstructed usage charts when delayed/backfilled events are replayed.

Context: We do frequent tenant reassignments across ingestion shards to rebalance load. When a migration happens close to a rate-limiter fixed-window boundary, the lease handoff logic can cause two behaviors: (1) transient acceptance of requests on the new shard while the old shard still holds short-lived window state, and (2) a path that treats excess requests as "dropped" (rate-limited) rather than buffered for retry. Downstream, our backfill replay job expects dropped tokens to be recorded in a "rate-limit-retry" stream; in this scenario those tokens are missing, leading to undercounts in per-model charts and quota reconciliations.

Impact: Affected tenants see a small undercount concentrated at window edges (typically 5-20 tokens per migration event) but it accumulates for busy tenants and shows up in monthly per-model leaderboards and quota reconciliations. Customer-facing severity: medium for most but high for a few large dedicated customers that trigger frequent migrations during scale events.

What we've done so far:
- Reproduced locally by simulating shard handoff at a fixed-window boundary with synthetic traffic (repro script in repo: infra/tests/rate_limit_migration_sim).
- Captured traces showing that requests that arrive within the last 200ms before the window boundary are sometimes flagged by handoff code path as "drop" instead of "retryable".
- Confirmed missing events in the reconstructed ledger: no corresponding rate-limit-retry entries for those requests, and downstream aggregator marks them as "unknown" origin.

Hypothesis: The migration handoff short-circuits the normal failure path for requests that would otherwise be enqueued for a retry (token bucket backoff). This is a logic gap in the handoff handshake; it treats the request as a final rejection because the old shard does not complete window state exchange fast enough.

Proposed fix: Update the handoff protocol to always tag last-second rejections with a "retryable:rate_limit" flag and forward minimal provenance metadata to the intake buffer so the backfill/ledger can recover them during shard replay. Concretely: (1) modify handoff ACK path to return code 429 with header X-RateLimit-Retryable=true for requests impacted by migration; (2) ensure the ingress gateway translates that into a guaranteed record in the rate-limit-retry stream; (3) add a reconciliation check in the backfill job to detect missing provenance and mark them for synthetic reconstruction if within a small window.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): Patch handoff code in staging and enable on 3 low-traffic tenants for 24h. Validate reconstructed usage against raw request logs.
- Stage 2 (pilot): Enable on 10 customers in region-us-east for 48h. Monitor Console per-model deltas and quota ledgers.
- Stage 3 (global): Default enable with feature flag, follow with sweep to reprocess any affected day ranges via a one-time backfill job.

Monitoring and success criteria:
- No net increase in 429s served to clients (we will prefer metadata tagging over client-visible changes).
- Backfill job should accept the retryable-tagged events and restore per-model counts to within 0.1% of raw request logs for sampled tenants.
- Console per-model heatmap should no longer show minute-edge dips during migrations for canary tenants.

Documentation and links:
- Reproduction script: https://git.internal.redwood/infrastructure/rate_limit_migration_sim (internal repo)
- Investigation notes and timeline: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/BILLING/Rate+Limiter+Migration+Edge+Case
- Proposed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2789 (WIP)
- Dashboard (canary metrics): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/usage-edgecases/rate-limit-migration

Next steps: finish PR, run canary, log results, and schedule one-time backfill window if validated.

Longer-term: evaluate moving to sliding-window rate-limiter or per-tenant rolling window with transfer-safe semantics to reduce boundary effects overall.
comments: 2025-03-04 Samira: Created ticket after two customer alerts and initial repro. Attached synthetic generator and trace captures.

2025-03-05 Liam: Local repro confirmed. Found that the handoff code path calls markDropped() when window_state==STALE and migration_in_progress==true. Drafting PR to change markDropped -> markRetryable for this code path.

2025-03-06 Engineering review (J. Huang): Suggest adding explicit provenance fields to the retry stream (tenant_id, model_id, trace_id) to ensure backfill can attribute correctly. Also add unit tests around window boundary behavior.

2025-03-07 QA (Maya): Ran canary in staging against 3 tenants for 12h. Reconstructed counts improved for 2 tenants; 1 tenant still had undercount — root cause was a separate ingress gateway drop; added ingress fix to the PR.

2025-03-08 Ops (Diego): Confirmed backfill job can ingest retryable records and restore missing ledger rows in test job. Prepared runbook for one-time backfill with start/end timestamps and estimated runtime.

2025-03-09 PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2789 includes ingress changes, additional provenance fields, and unit tests. Requesting review from runtime and billing owners.
2025-03-10 Samira: Marking this ticket In Progress -> next action is schedule pilot in us-east and monitor per-model delta panels. Liam to coordinate rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Canary tenants show no minute-edge undercount compared to raw request logs (sampled).
Backfill job can consume retryable-tagged records and restore ledger entries for a sample day within SLA.
Unit and integration tests cover window boundary and migration handoff logic to prevent regressions.
